title: Engineering Drawing and Spec Sheet Extraction
summary: Extract title blocks, dimensions, tolerances, GD&T, materials and notes from 2D drawings and spec sheets for faster RFQ review, ballooned inspection plans and revision checks.

seo.title: Engineering Drawing Data Extraction with AI | VipraTech
seo.description: AI reads 2D drawings and spec sheets, extracts title blocks, dimensions, tolerances and GD&T, builds balloon lists and flags revision changes.

problem.intro: Every RFQ, new part introduction and engineering change starts with someone reading a drawing line by line. Estimators hunt for material, finish and tight tolerances, quality engineers balloon every characteristic for first article inspection, and changes between revisions are found by eye.

pain_points.title: Slow RFQ turnaround
pain_points.detail: Estimators read each customer drawing to find material grade, heat treatment, surface finish and critical tolerances before they can cost the part.

pain_points.title: Manual ballooning
pain_points.detail: Numbering every dimension and note for PPAP or first article inspection reports is slow, repetitive work in PDF tools.

pain_points.title: Missed revision changes
pain_points.detail: A tolerance tightened between revision B and C is easy to miss, and the old value ends up in the control plan or the CNC program.

pain_points.title: Unsearchable legacy drawings
pain_points.detail: Decades of scanned drawings sit in folders, so finding every part made from a given material or with a given thread is guesswork.

solution.overview: We build a drawing reader that locates the title block, views and notes on each sheet, then extracts dimensions with tolerances, GD&T feature control frames, surface finish symbols, threads, material and heat treatment notes. Each characteristic gets a balloon number and a link to its location on the drawing. The output can feed an RFQ checklist, an inspection plan template or an item master entry in your ERP. When a new revision arrives, the system compares it with the previous one and lists added, removed and changed characteristics. Engineers confirm the extraction before any of it is used.
capabilities: Reads title block fields such as part number, drawing number, revision, material and general tolerance standard
Extracts linear and angular dimensions with tolerances, fits and thread callouts
Detects GD&T feature control frames, datums and surface finish symbols
Builds a ballooned characteristic list and fills your FAI or inspection report template
Compares revisions and lists added, removed and changed characteristics
Indexes legacy drawings so engineers can search by material, feature or note

workflow.title: Receive drawings
workflow.detail: Drawings arrive as PDFs, TIFF scans or exported sheets from the RFQ mailbox or PLM vault.

workflow.title: Detect layout
workflow.detail: A vision model finds the title block, views, tables and note areas on each sheet.

workflow.title: Extract characteristics
workflow.detail: OCR and an LLM read dimensions, tolerances, GD&T, threads and notes, each with a confidence score and location.

workflow.title: Engineer verification
workflow.detail: Low-confidence and critical characteristics are highlighted for the engineer to confirm on the drawing.

workflow.title: Compare with previous revision
workflow.detail: Where an earlier revision exists, changes are listed characteristic by characteristic.

workflow.title: Publish outputs
workflow.detail: The verified list feeds the RFQ checklist, ballooned drawing, inspection plan or ERP item master.

inputs: 2D drawings as PDF, TIFF or scanned sheets
Customer and internal material and finish spec sheets
Previous drawing revisions from the PLM vault or folders
Your FAI, PPAP or inspection report templates
outputs: Structured title block and characteristic list per drawing
Ballooned drawing and a filled inspection report draft
Revision change list between drawing versions
RFQ checklist of material, finish, critical tolerances and special processes
human_in_the_loop: A design or quality engineer verifies every characteristic flagged as critical or low-confidence on a drawing overlay before the list is used. Nothing extracted goes into a quote, control plan or CNC program without that sign-off.
integrations: PLM or PDM vault such as Windchill, Teamcenter or SolidWorks PDM
guardrails: Every value linked to its location on the drawing
Critical characteristics always shown for engineer confirmation
Drawings processed in your tenancy or on-premise to respect customer NDAs
Only the released revision is used for outputs
compliance_notes: Customer drawings are often under NDA or export-control terms; processing can stay on-premise and specific programmes can be excluded.
Outputs can support PPAP and first article inspection records, including AS9102-style reports in aerospace, with engineers retaining sign-off.

pilot.scope: One drawing family, such as machined or sheet-metal parts, using recent RFQ and production drawings from two or three customers.
deliverables: Characteristic schema and output templates agreed with engineering
Working extraction on a set of your real drawings

Changes found by the comparison engine against a manual comparison of sample revision pairs.

faqs.q: Can it read old scanned drawings with poor line quality?
faqs.a: Yes, within limits. Faded or skewed scans are cleaned up before reading, and any region the system cannot read with confidence is flagged rather than guessed. The pilot report separates accuracy for native PDFs and scans.

faqs.q: Does it understand GD&T, or just read the text?
faqs.a: It detects feature control frames and reads the symbol, tolerance value, modifiers and datum references as structured fields. Interpreting what a callout means for your process stays with your engineers.

faqs.q: Can we work from CAD models instead of 2D drawings?
faqs.a: Where you have native CAD with PMI, extracting from the model is often better, and we can discuss it. Most suppliers still receive 2D drawings with RFQs, which is where this system helps most.

faqs.q: Customer drawings are confidential. Where are they processed?
faqs.a: In your cloud tenancy or on a server in your plant. We use model endpoints that do not retain data, and specific customers or programmes can be excluded entirely.
